newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dutch KPN wins outright control of transport firm TNT.
newsitem.headline: Dutch KPN wins outright control of transport firm TNT.

text.p: The postal unit of Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said Friday it won majority control of transport giant TNT Ltd. after Bankers Trust finally agreed to sell its stake for a tidy profit.

Bankers Trust Australia Ltd., a unit of the Wall Street firm, had refused to tender its 19.9 percent stake in the Australian company to KPN, arguing that the A$2.45 ($1.98) per share offer worth a total of A$2 billion ($1.62 billion) was too low.

Announcing that Bankers Trust finally agreed to tender its 105 million TNT shares -- giving KPN a stake of 51.9 percent -- the Dutch company freed the friendly bid from all conditions and extended the closing date of the offer to Dec. 12.
"Now that we're over 50 percent and Bankers Trust have tendered their shares that will take a big obstacle away," said PTT Post head Ad Scheepbouwer in a telephone interview.

"Until yesterday, we were a bidder, now we're the majority shareholder and we have to look at more detailed information -- until now not available to us -- and to see which of those businesses fit within our focus."

KPN wants 100 percent ownership of TNT, its partner in the GD Express business in Europe, and had said the friendly bid launched in early October would not be valid unless at least 90 percent of TNT shares were tendered.

Bankers Trust held about 16 percent of TNT before the bid was launched and bought another 18 million shares between A$2.38 ($1.93) and A$2.43 ($1.97) per share afterwards, apparently to force KPN or another potential suitor to raise its price, fund managers said.

Analysts said there was never much chance that KPN's bid would be matched by another express freight firm such as Federal Express Corp., once seen as a possible suitor, because KPN's offer was exceedingly generous for a company which had struggled financially in recent years.
The head of investment at a leading institution said he now expected other fund managers to quickly accept the KPN offer.
An adviser to KPN, who asked not to be identified, said KPN hoped to quickly gain outright control of TNT and begin the promised strategic review of assets as soon as possible.
"We are confident that now KPN has control that shareholders will see the value of the offer and accept," the adviser said.
TNT shares traded at A$1.63 ($2.01) the day before the bid was announced at a joint news conference on Oct. 2.
The bid has received regulatory approval from officials in Australia, Europe and the United States.
Scheepbouwer said the immediate job in hand would be to integrate in those areas where there was most duplication of activities -- the Netherlands, Australia, Italy, Germany and Britain.
"Once we are an integrated company, which has its absolute strength in Europe, Asia and the Middle East, that's when we will capitalise on our economies of scale and gain more market share," he said.
Scheepbouwer said it was too early to say which businesses would be sold off during the integration or discuss the scale of any potential job losses.

"No doubt there will be some businesses that don't (fit in the new structure), no doubt we will find other solutions for those businesses. At the moment there's probably more of those businesses outside Europe than inside," he said.
Analysts expect KPN to consider the sale of TNT's Asian operations as well as its half share in the AWAS aircraft leasing operation.
